# Installation

> Get a working design system on your screen, from an empty folder, in about five minutes.
>
> **This is the Markdown mirror.** The [interactive version](../02-installation.html) has live
> widgets — a brand switch, an alias-chain walker, a pipeline stepper, and a quiz — that
> Markdown cannot render.

← [The idea](01-the-idea.md)  ·  [Contents](README.md)  ·  [How it works](03-how-it-works.md) →

---

Two paths. Path A explores the example workspace in this repository and takes about two minutes;
it is the fastest way to see what girih produces. Path B scaffolds a workspace of your own. Do A
first even if you want B.

## Before you start

| You need | Version | Check with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node.js | 20 or newer | `node --version` |
| pnpm | 11.8.0 (this repo pins it) | `pnpm --version` |
| git | any recent | `git --version` |

pnpm is pinned through the `packageManager` field, so if you have corepack enabled the
right version is used automatically. If you do not have pnpm at all:

**[Terminal]**

```
corepack enable          # ships with Node 20+, easiest route
# or:
npm install -g pnpm@11.8.0
```

> **🟡 Watch out — Why pnpm specifically**
>
> This is a workspace monorepo where the example app depends on the packages by
> `workspace:*`, and the end-to-end test packs real tarballs and installs them into a
> scratch consumer. npm and yarn can host workspaces too, but the lockfile here is pnpm's and the
> scripts assume its layout. Use pnpm for the repo; your own _consuming_ app can use
> whatever it likes.

## A note on installing

> **🔴 Important — Nothing is published to npm yet**
>
> Every package in this repository is at version `0.1.0` and has never been published.
> `npm install @girih/cli` will not work today, and neither will
> `npx create-girih`. Both are wired and tested — the end-to-end suite packs real
> tarballs and installs them into a fresh consumer — but the publish has not happened. Until it
> does, you build from source, which is what both paths below do.

## Path A: explore this repo

**[Terminal]**

```
git clone <this-repo> girih
cd girih
pnpm install
pnpm build            # tsup builds every package into dist/
```

`pnpm build` is required before anything else, because the CLI you are about to run is
the compiled one in `packages/cli/dist/cli.js`. Now compile the example design system:

**[Terminal]**

```
cd examples/acme-ds

pnpm check            # validate tokens + contracts, print the resolved token table
pnpm run demo:react   # generate the React package, then bundle the demo
open demo/react/index.html
```

That last page is a variant matrix with a live brand toggle. Flip it and watch the corner radius
change along with the colour — that is the three-tier cascade doing its job, and
[chapter 04](04-tokens.md) explains exactly why.

There is also a no-framework demo, which is worth opening because it proves the mechanism needs
no React at all:

**[Terminal]**

```
open demo/index.html   # plain HTML + the generated tokens.css, no bundler
```

## Path B: start your own workspace

`create-girih` scaffolds a working workspace — tokens in three tiers, one Button
contract, and a demo page that needs no build step. Run it from the built binary:

**[Terminal]**

```
# from the root of this repo, after pnpm build
node packages/create-girih/dist/cli.js my-ds --workspace

cd my-ds
pnpm install
pnpm exec girih generate react
open demo/index.html
```

The `--workspace` flag makes the new directory a pnpm workspace that links back to
this repo's packages, which is what you want while nothing is on npm. Once published, the same
thing becomes `npx create-girih my-ds` with no flag.

If you would rather add girih to a directory that already exists, use `girih init`
instead. It refuses to run if a config file is already present, and warns you if an ancestor
directory is already a girih workspace:

**[Terminal]**

```
cd existing-project
pnpm exec girih init --name @acme/design-system --brand main
```

> **🟢 In plain words**
>
> `create-girih` makes a new folder from nothing. `girih init` adds girih to
> a folder you are already standing in. Same result, different starting point.

---

## Your first generate

Here is what `girih generate react` actually prints. Every line is a file written, with
its byte count — girih is deliberately loud about what it touched:

**[Terminal]**

```
$ pnpm exec girih generate react

write  packages/design-system/styles/tokens.css (6721 bytes)
write  packages/design-system/styles/components.css (6402 bytes)
write  packages/design-system/src/Button.tsx (1187 bytes)
write  packages/design-system/src/index.ts (612 bytes)
write  packages/design-system/package.json (694 bytes)
write  .ds/ir/ (6 component IR files)

Preview: open demo/index.html · usage: packages/design-system/README.md
```

Four things were produced, and it is worth knowing which is which:

| Output | What it is | Committed? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `styles/tokens.css` | Every token as a CSS custom property, with a scoped block per brand | No — regenerable |
| `styles/components.css` | Component structure only; every design value is a `var()` | No — regenerable |
| `src/*.tsx` | Typed React components, one per contract | No — regenerable |
| `.ds/ir/*.json` | Canonical contract form, target-neutral | **Yes** — it is the reviewable contract |
| `.ds/manifest.json` | SHA-256 per emitted file, for drift detection | **Yes** — it is the safety net |

> **🔵 Rule — Do not edit anything under packages/design-system/**
>
> It is a build artifact. girih records a hash of every file it writes, and the next
> `generate` will refuse to run if it finds a hand edit — naming the file and telling
> you to either undo the change or `girih eject` the component. That refusal is the
> feature. If you find yourself wanting to edit the output, the thing you actually want to change
> is a token or a contract.

## Using the package in an app

The generated package is an ordinary npm package. In your application, import the two stylesheets
once and the components wherever you need them:

**your app  [You write this]**

```tsx
import '@acme/design-system/styles/tokens.css';
import '@acme/design-system/styles/components.css';
import { Button, BrandProvider } from '@acme/design-system';

export function Checkout() {
  return (
    <BrandProvider brand="seller">
      <Button variant="primary" size="lg">Pay now</Button>
    </BrandProvider>
  );
}
```

`BrandProvider` renders a wrapper carrying `data-brand="seller"`. That is
the entire runtime — everything else is CSS resolving in the browser. Nest providers and the inner
one wins, at any depth, which is why the CSS emitter goes to the trouble of re-declaring the
dependents closure in each brand's scope.

<details>
<summary><b>The order of those two imports matters — here is why</b></summary>

`tokens.css` defines the custom properties; `components.css` consumes them.
CSS custom properties do not care about declaration order the way normal properties do — a
`var()` is resolved at use time, not at parse time — so in practice either order
works. Import tokens first anyway: it matches the dependency direction, and it means a reader
scanning your entry file sees values before use.

What _does_ matter is that both are imported exactly once, at the application root. The
generated `package.json` marks CSS as having side effects
(`"sideEffects": ["**/*.css"]`) so bundlers do not tree-shake the imports away.

</details>

## Every command

| Command | What it does | Writes? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `girih init` | Scaffold a workspace in the current directory | Yes |
| `girih brand create ` | Add a brand overlay and register it in `ds.config.ts` | Yes |
| `girih check` | Validate tokens, brands, contracts, extensions; print the token table | No |
| `girih generate css` | Emit `tokens.css` + `tokens.d.ts` | Yes |
| `girih generate react` | Emit the whole React package plus canonical IR | Yes |
| `girih generate react --check` | Verify the output on disk is current. The CI gate. | **No** |
| `girih eject ` | Convert one generated component into a tracked fork | Yes |
| `girih build` | Compile the generated package to publishable `dist/` | Yes |
| `girih publish` | Derive the semver bump from the contract diff and publish | Dry run by default |
| `girih update` | Report ejected forks that drifted from current templates | No |

> **🟡 Watch out — Two flags to be careful with**
>
> `girih generate --force` overwrites hand-edited output. That is precisely the work
> the drift gate exists to protect, so reach for `girih eject` first — it carries the
> hand edits into a tracked fork rather than discarding them.
>
> `girih publish --yes` is the only irreversible command here. Without
> `--yes` it stages the package, prints the version diff, runs
> `npm publish --dry-run`, and cleans up. Read that output before adding the flag.

## When it does not work

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `` run `pnpm build` before the consumer e2e `` | The CLI in `dist/` does not exist yet | `pnpm build` from the repo root |
| `girih: command not found` | The binary is workspace-local, not global | Use `pnpm exec girih …` from inside the workspace |
| `GIRIH1001` — no config found | You are not in a girih workspace | `cd` to the directory containing `ds.config.ts` |
| `GIRIH2006` — no token files matched | Empty or misnamed `tokens/` | Create `tokens/global.tokens.json`; the tier comes from the filename |
| `GIRIH1010` — file edited by hand | Someone edited generated output | Undo it, or `girih eject` the component to keep the edits |
| Brand switch changes colour but not radius | A brand block is missing part of the dependents closure | Regenerate. If it persists it is a generator bug — see [chapter 06](06-the-code.md) |
| `ENOENT … e2e/.tmp/consumer/app/smoke.mjs` | Known flake: two e2e files share `e2e/.tmp` and one deletes it in teardown | Re-run. It passes in isolation with `pnpm vitest run e2e/test/consumer.test.ts` |

Every diagnostic girih can emit is listed in [chapter 07](07-error-codes.md),
extracted directly from the source. If you got a code that is not there, the reference is stale —
re-run `node docs/scripts/extract-diagnostics.mjs`.

Something is on your screen now. [Chapter 03](03-how-it-works.md) explains what
happened when you pressed enter.
